name: Coder

plans.name: Community
plans.note: Open source (AGPL-3.0), self-hosted; unlimited workspaces and users; Coder Agents limited to 5 concurrently active agents per deployment (extra agents queue). Licence $0; the customer pays their own infrastructure (modes stay unpriced).

plans.name: Premium
plans.note: Priced 'Annually per user'; no number published (Get a demo). A seat = a user active in the last 90 days. Adds HA, workspace proxies, external provisioners, prebuilt workspaces, audit logging, groups/multi-org RBAC, resource quotas, AI Gateway + Agent Firewall (AI Governance), SLA support. Still 5 concurrent Coder Agents. 30-day free trial.

plans.name: AI Premium
plans.note: 'Custom'. Everything in Premium plus unlimited concurrent Coder Agents, metered against a purchased pool of 'Agent Time' (cumulative LLM-invocation time, reported hourly to Coder's Tallyman/Metronome). When Agent Time runs out the deployment falls back to the concurrency cap.

caveats: Self-hosted cloud-development workspace product. Coder provisions customer-selected infrastructure; licence is not a compute price. Free open-source and commercial Premium options exist.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

Coder Agents concurrency: Community and Premium allow 5 concurrently active agents per deployment (extra agents queue); AI Premium removes the cap but meters 'Agent Time' (LLM invocation time) from a purchased pool, reported hourly to Coder (tallyman-prod.coder.com) - outbound reporting required unless arranged otherwise.
Premium seats are counted as users active in the last 90 days (dormant users do not consume seats).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Stopped: Ephemeral resources destroyed, persistent resources idle
snapshot_auto.note: Stop (manual, schedule or inactivity autostop) runs Terraform to destroy ephemeral resources; only template-defined persistent resources (e.g. home volume) survive. No memory/process save and no Coder-level snapshot. Anything more depends on the customer's infrastructure.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: coder [global-flags] <subcommand> ... login | notifications | oauth2-provider | port-forward | publickey | version | whoami | support | server | prebuilds
snapshot_on_demand.note: Full Coder CLI/API command surface has no snapshot or checkpoint command. The only 'state' command is 'Manually manage Terraform state to fix broken workspaces' (state pull/push of the Terraform state file, not a disk/VM snapshot). Coder's own docs describe workspace stop as destroying ephemeral Terraform resources and idling persistent ones (workspace-lifecycle.md) - no on-demand snapshot/checkpoint concept anywhere in the CLI reference, REST API reference, or docs index. Any actual disk snapshot capability would come from the customer's underlying cloud/Terraform provider outside Coder, confirming the card's 'no' for a first-party on-demand snapshot API.

harness_api.quote: Coder Agents is a chat interface and API for delegating development work and research to coding agents in your Coder deployment.
harness_api.note: Harness: Coder's own Go agent ('coder-agents'). Chats API (/api/v2/chats; some endpoints /api/experimental): create chat with prompt, WebSocket stream, follow-up messages, interrupt, list/archive chats, sub-agents. Nuance: the agent loop runs in the Coder control plane and drives the workspace as its tool target, not a harness process inside the workspace. The older Tasks API (Claude Code/Codex/etc. inside the workspace via AgentAPI) is deprecated since v2.36 and 'no longer available by default'; coder/agentapi (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Goose, Aider, Amp, Copilot, Cursor CLI...) is archived/deprecated. Premium/licensed feature ('Agent Time' usage).

egress_allowlist.quote: Agent Firewall offers network policy enforcement, which blocks domains and HTTP verbs to prevent exfiltration, and writes logs to the workspace.
egress_allowlist.note: Agent Firewall (ex 'Agent Boundaries', Premium AI Governance) is a process-level jail inside the workspace (nsjail: netns+veth+iptables, needs CAP_NET_ADMIN; or landjail/Landlock), so it constrains the wrapped agent process, not a root user of the workspace; audit logs stream to the control plane. Machine-level egress (IP/CIDR) is whatever the template's infra provides, e.g. a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy created by the template (agent-isolation guide on main branch). Not a Coder-hosted network edge.

egress_http_rules.quote: `method=POST domain=api.example.com path=/users,/posts` - allows specific methods, domain, and paths
egress_http_rules.note: Agent Firewall rules engine: domain / method / path keys (no header rules documented). Same in-workspace process-jail caveat as above.

ingress_rules.quote: `owner` (Default): The implicit sharing level for all listening ports, only visible to the workspace owner
ingress_rules.note: Port share levels owner / organization / authenticated / public per port; admins can cap the maximum share level per template (Owner disables sharing). Access otherwise via authenticated Coder tunnel (coder port-forward/SSH/Desktop). Infra-level inbound (security groups etc.) is up to the template.

guest_firewall.note: Template-dependent: VM-based templates give full root; container templates need CAP_NET_ADMIN. Coder's own Agent Firewall nsjail mode uses iptables in a netns inside the workspace and 'Requires CAP_NET_ADMIN', showing it works when the template grants it.

secret_proxy.quote: Users use their Coder session or API tokens to authenticate with `coderd`, and `coderd` securely communicates with the upstream APIs on their behalf.
secret_proxy.note: AI Gateway (ex AI Bridge, Premium): OpenAI/Anthropic-style provider keys held centrally in coderd; the workspace holds only a Coder token (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<coder token>). AI Gateway Proxy covers tools without base-URL override. Coder Agents keeps LLM keys in the control plane ('never enters the workspace'). General user secrets / Vault / external-auth tokens are injected into the workspace as env vars or files ("Anyone with shell or file access to a workspace can read secrets injected"). Git SSH keys are fetched on demand into memory, not a proxy.

volume_attach.quote: To make Homebrew survive a restart, you'll edit the template and add a persistent volume.
volume_attach.note: Volumes are declared in Terraform templates on the customer's infrastructure (docker_volume, Kubernetes PVC, cloud disks); Coder does not sell storage itself.

image_oci.quote: Your image(s) (e.g. a Docker image with languages and tools installed).
image_oci.note: Docker/OCI-based templates let workspaces start from a customer-supplied image; also supports Envbuilder/devcontainers to build from a Dockerfile.

browser.quote: Coder Workspaces: Self-hosted cloud development environments for your developers and their agents.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Coder is a dev-environment/IDE-access platform (web terminal, SSH, IDEs, optional VNC/RDP desktop apps); it does not ship or manage a browser instance as a product feature.

computer_use.quote: Coder Workspaces: Self-hosted cloud development environments for your developers and their agents.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No screenshot+click computer-use API exists in the docs; Coder's agent APIs (Coder Agents) drive a coding harness via chat/tool-calls, not screen-level control.

anti_bot.quote: Coder Workspaces: Self-hosted cloud development environments for your developers and their agents.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Coder is a dev-environment orchestrator, not a browser-automation/scraping product; no stealth/fingerprinting feature exists.

captcha_solving.quote: Coder Workspaces: Self-hosted cloud development environments for your developers and their agents.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

ssh.quote: Coder will use the optimal path for an SSH connection ... when using the CLI: `coder ssh my-workspace`

snapshot.quote: Stopped: Ephemeral resources destroyed, persistent resources idle
snapshot.note: Stopping a workspace runs Terraform to destroy ephemeral resources; only template-declared persistent resources (e.g. a home volume) survive. There is no Coder-level disk or memory snapshot/checkpoint concept in the docs, REST API, or CLI reference.

fork.quote: Coder templates have full control over workspace ephemerality.
fork.note: No 'clone/fork an existing workspace' feature is documented; users create new workspaces from a template/parameters, not by duplicating a live workspace's state.

fork_running.quote: Templates ... define the underlying infrastructure that all Coder workspaces run on.
fork_running.note: No documented capability to clone a running workspace without stopping it; follows from fork being unsupported.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Stopped: Ephemeral resources destroyed, persistent resources idle
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory-inclusive clone/snapshot mechanism exists; follows from snapshot=none and fork=false.

pause_resume.quote: Stopped: Ephemeral resources destroyed, persistent resources idle
pause_resume.note: Workspaces can be stopped and later started again (manually, on a schedule, or via inactivity autostop); compute billing/usage stops while stopped since ephemeral resources are destroyed, though this is a stop/start of infra rather than an in-memory pause.

wake_on_request.quote: Stopped: Ephemeral resources destroyed, persistent resources idle
wake_on_request.note: A stopped workspace must be explicitly started (UI/CLI/API) or hit a scheduled autostart time; the docs describe no mechanism that wakes a stopped workspace automatically the moment an inbound request/connection arrives.

persistent_disk.quote: By default, all Coder resources are persistent, but production templates must use the practices laid out in this document to prevent accidental deletion.
persistent_disk.note: Template-declared volumes (e.g. home directory) survive stop/start.

volume_shared.note: Native templates provision one persistent volume per workspace; there is no documented Coder feature for mounting a single volume simultaneously across several running workspaces (would require a customer-built NFS-style template, outside Coder's own feature set).

live_resize.quote: Additional parameters (e.g. disk size, instance type, or region).
live_resize.note: Changing CPU/RAM/instance-type template parameters triggers a workspace rebuild (stop and recreate the compute resource), not a live in-place resize of a running machine.

own_agent_api.quote: Coder Agents is a chat interface and API for delegating development work and research to coding agents in your Coder deployment.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Coder's own API/product ('Coder Agents') drives a coding harness (chat/tool-calls against a dev workspace), not a browser/computer-use/research agent product distinct from coding.

lang_python.quote: Your image(s) (e.g. a Docker image with languages and tools installed).
lang_python.note: Runtime languages depend on the chosen workspace image/template, but Coder's official starter templates and registry modules (e.g. Docker base images, devcontainers) commonly ship Python out of the box.

lang_node.quote: Your image(s) (e.g. a Docker image with languages and tools installed).
lang_node.note: Same as lang_python: depends on the template image, but Node.js is included in Coder's common starter templates/registry modules (e.g. code-server, VS Code Web modules).

public_ipv4.quote: There are many ways to connect to your workspace, the options are only limited by the template configuration.
public_ipv4.note: Coder's own access model is a proxied/tunnelled connection (coderd reverse proxy, workspace apps subdomains, Coder Connect/Tailscale-based networking, SSH) rather than assigning a public IPv4 address per workspace; any raw public IP would come from the underlying cloud template, not Coder.

inbound_https.quote: `owner` (Default): The implicit sharing level for all listening ports, only visible to the workspace owner
inbound_https.note: Ports on a workspace are exposed as HTTPS workspace-app URLs through the Coder server, with configurable share levels (owner/organization/authenticated/public).

static_egress_ip.quote: Templates ... define the underlying infrastructure that all Coder workspaces run on.
static_egress_ip.note: No Coder-level fixed outbound IP feature is documented; any static egress IP would have to be configured in the customer's own template/cloud network, not provided by Coder itself.

gpu.quote: Additional parameters (e.g. disk size, instance type, or region).
gpu.note: Coder templates commonly select GPU-backed instance types on the target cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure/K8s GPU node pools); GPU workspace templates are a standard documented pattern in Coder's registry and tutorials.

arm64.note: Coder ships arm64 server/CLI/agent binaries for Linux and macOS; workspaces can likewise run on arm64 infrastructure via templates.

hipaa.quote: Coder is an enterprise platform for deploying self-hosted development environments and AI coding agents on governed infrastructure, giving platform teams centralized control over security, models, and spend.
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Coder's trust page advertises SOC 2 Type II certification but makes no HIPAA-eligibility or BAA claim; as a self-hosted product, HIPAA compliance of the deployment is the customer's own infrastructure responsibility, not a Coder-provided attestation.

eu_data_residency.quote: Templates ... define the underlying infrastructure that all Coder workspaces run on.
eu_data_residency.note: Because Coder is self-hosted, the control plane and all workspace data can be deployed entirely inside EU infrastructure chosen by the customer; no page states an EU restriction, and this follows directly from the self-hosted architecture.

max_session_h.quote: In a completely persistent workspace, there is no difference between the Off and On states.
max_session_h.note: Coder workspaces are long-running dev VMs/containers with no built-in maximum session duration; they run until stopped by the user, an admin-configured autostop schedule, or inactivity timeout, not a fixed session cap.

usage_api.quote: Workspace API returns workspace objects with daily_cost field per workspace. GET /api/v2/users/{user}/workspace/{workspacename} and workspace listing endpoints include daily_cost for billable usage tracking per sandbox.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; Coder's REST API Workspaces endpoints return individual workspace metadata including daily_cost, enabling per-workspace usage tracking. Premium Quotas feature adds credit-based cost management and spend limits per user/organization.

locations_quote: Coder is an enterprise platform for deploying self-hosted development environments and AI coding agents on governed infrastructure
